findings.summary: The purchase is inside the mandate that was in force when it was made.

The mandate says 'Whole bean, never ground.' The agent ordered 'Decaf, ground, 340 g', which breaks that instruction even though it fits the spending scope. The decaf choice is consistent with the second instruction about avoiding caffeine.

The ordered item is described as ground, and the buyer says the delivered bag is ground. What was delivered appears to match what was ordered and described. The problem lies in what the agent chose, not in the merchant's fulfilment.

evidence_notes.text: The purchase was made by the buyer's AI agent and falls inside the mandate in force at the time: one approved merchant, the coffee beans category, and a cap of 40.00 USD against a disputed amount of 16.00 USD.
The mandate instructed 'Whole bean, never ground.' The agent ordered 'Decaf, ground, 340 g', which contradicts that instruction.
The decaf selection is consistent with the buyer's instruction that caffeine keeps their partner up.
USPS tracking 9400111899223857216617 shows the shipment as delivered.
The buyer confirms the bag received is ground. That matches the order description, so there is no indication the merchant shipped something other than what was ordered.
Although the dispute reason is 'not as described', the facts point to an agent instruction violation rather than a listing or fulfilment discrepancy.

buyer_message.text: We reviewed your case. Your instructions to your shopping assistant said whole bean, never ground.
The order your assistant placed was for 'Decaf, ground, 340 g', so the ground coffee you received is what was ordered.
Your assistant did choose decaf, which fits your note about caffeine in the evening, but choosing ground coffee went against your whole-bean instruction.
Our records show the package was delivered by USPS, tracking number 9400111899223857216617.
We have passed these findings to PayPal's reviewer, who will decide the outcome of your refund request.
